topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer-causing mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising within cells can support cancer evolution in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental exposure and the interpretation of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and how evidence for that contribution should be interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the relationship between infection and malignant transformation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmental mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental agents produce DNA damage and mutations, with their effects depending on activation and the tissue environment.

topics.label: Tumour promotion beyond mutagenic initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why mutagenic initiation may be insufficient for cancer and how promoter activity enables initiated cells to grow into tumours.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue susceptibility, with a recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how carcinogenic effects depend on the susceptible host tissue and place that specificity within a recap of the mechanisms already discussed.

topics.label: Methods and limitations of assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence is gathered to identify carcinogenic exposures and why the available methods cannot fully establish their effects in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing everyday exposure decisions as balances of risks and benefits.
